clips.send: Hainan Island. Hainan Province; tropical. About 34,000 square kilometers — China’s second-largest island. Tropical all year: coconut palms, beaches and rubber trees. Sanya is on its southern tip. Hainan Province also governs the South China Sea Islands.

clips.send: Dongsha Islands. The northernmost of the four island groups. Coral islands and reefs southeast of Guangdong. The South China Sea Islands are four groups: Dongsha, Xisha, Zhongsha and Nansha (East, West, Middle and South Sands).

clips.send: South China Sea. China’s largest and deepest sea. About 3.5 million square kilometers — more than a third the size of the whole United States. Deep: about 1,200 m on average, over 5,000 m (16,400 ft) at its deepest. Warm and tropical, full of coral reefs. The South China Sea Islands are coral islands. One of the world’s busiest shipping routes, with rich oil and gas.

clips.send: Yellow Sea. Between the mainland and the Korean Peninsula. Named for its yellowish water: rivers once carried huge loads of yellow silt into it. Average depth about 44 m (144 ft) — still shallow. Big ports on its coast: Dalian and Qingdao. Off the Jiangsu coast there is a maze of sand ridges — a famous hazard for ships.

clips.send: Zhoushan Islands. Off the coast of Zhejiang. China’s largest archipelago (island group), with over a thousand islands. Next to the Zhoushan fishing ground, China’s biggest. Part of the giant Ningbo–Zhoushan Port.

clips.send: Chongming Island. An alluvial island at the mouth of the Yangtze. Built by the river itself: mud and sand dropped by the Yangtze piled up into an island (an alluvial island, 冲积岛). About 1,200 square kilometers — roughly the size of the city of Los Angeles — and still growing. Part of Shanghai.

clips.send: Taiwan Island. China’s largest island; part of Taiwan Province. About 36,000 square kilometers — a bit bigger than Maryland. Tall mountains run down its spine: Yushan (Jade Mountain), 3,952 m, is the highest peak in eastern China. Tropical in the south, subtropical in the north.

clips.send: Zhongsha Islands. Mostly underwater banks and reefs. Most of the Zhongsha Islands are coral banks below the surface. Huangyan Island (黄岩岛) is the part that rises above the sea.

clips.send: East China Sea. A wide, shallow continental shelf. Stretches from the Yangtze mouth south to a line between Nan’ao Island (Guangdong) and the southern tip of Taiwan. A wide continental shelf: shallow water rich in fish, oil and gas. The Yangtze, Asia’s longest river, empties into it near Shanghai. The Zhoushan fishing ground — China’s largest — is here, and so are the Diaoyu Islands.

clips.send: Bohai Sea. Almost surrounded by land. An inland sea (内海): land wraps around it on three sides — Liaoning, Hebei, Tianjin and Shandong. Very shallow: about 18 m (60 ft) deep on average — a six-storey building would stick out. About 77,000 square kilometers , a bit smaller than South Carolina. Its northern part freezes in winter. The Yellow River (Huang He) flows into it; its coast has China’s biggest offshore oilfield and the Changlu salt fields.

clips.send: Qiongzhou Strait. Between the Leizhou Peninsula and Hainan Island. Counts as an inland sea of China, like the Bohai. Only about 20–40 km (12–25 miles) wide. Trains cross it on ferries: whole railway carriages roll onto ships.

clips.send: Diaoyu Islands. Northeast of Taiwan Island, in the East China Sea. A small group of islands about 170 km (105 miles) northeast of Taiwan Island. Diaoyu Dao, the main island, is about 4 square kilometers — about the size of New York’s Central Park. China’s textbooks teach that the Diaoyu Islands are China’s inherent territory, attached to Taiwan Province, and standard Chinese maps always show them.

clips.send: Xisha Islands. Southeast of Hainan Island. Coral islands with white sand and clear water. Yongxing Island here is the largest island of the South China Sea Islands and the seat of Sansha City (三沙市), part of Hainan Province.

clips.send: Taiwan Strait. Between Fujian Province and Taiwan Island. China’s largest strait, linking the East China Sea and the South China Sea. About 130 km (80 miles) at its narrowest — a bit narrower than the Straits of Florida. Shallow: about 60 m deep on average, with the even shallower Taiwan Banks in the south-west.

clips.send: Bohai Strait. Between the Liaodong and Shandong Peninsulas. The doorway between the Bohai and the Yellow Sea. About 106 km (66 miles) across at its narrowest. The Miaodao Islands (庙岛群岛) sit across it like stepping stones.

clips.send: 黄海。位于我国大陆与朝鲜半岛之间。历史上河流带来大量泥沙，海水呈黄色，因而得名。。平均深度约44米。。沿岸有大连、青岛等大港。。江苏沿岸有大片辐射状沙脊（苏北浅滩），船舶要小心。

clips.send: 舟山群岛。位于浙江沿海。我国最大的群岛，有一千多个岛屿。。附近是我国最大的渔场——舟山渔场。。属于宁波舟山港的一部分。

clips.send: 南海。我国面积最大、最深的海。面积约350万平方千米。。平均深度约1200米，最深处超过5000米。。地处热带，多珊瑚礁；南海诸岛是珊瑚岛。。是重要的海上航道，油气资源丰富。

clips.send: 曾母暗沙。约北纬4 度 ，属南沙群岛。我国领土的最南端，约北纬4 度 。。“暗沙”是隐没在水下的沙滩，它位于海面以下约20米。。从最北端漠河附近（约北纬53 度 ）到这里，南北跨纬度近50度。

clips.send: 崇明岛。长江口的冲积岛。由长江带来的泥沙堆积而成，是我国最大的冲积岛。。面积约1200平方千米，而且还在不断“长大”。。属于上海市。

clips.send: 南沙群岛。位置最南、分布最广。四大群岛中分布海域最广，岛、礁、沙、滩众多。。我国领土的最南端——曾母暗沙就在南沙群岛。

clips.send: 钓鱼岛及其附属岛屿。位于台湾岛东北，在东海。位于台湾岛东北约170千米的东海海域。。主岛钓鱼岛面积约4平方千米。。钓鱼岛及其附属岛屿是台湾的附属岛屿，自古以来就是中国的固有领土，标准地图上必须标出。

clips.send: 东海。大陆架宽广。北起长江口北岸，南至广东南澳岛与台湾岛南端的连线。。大陆架宽广，渔业和油气资源丰富。。长江在上海附近注入东海。。我国最大的渔场——舟山渔场在这里；钓鱼岛也位于东海。

clips.send: 台湾岛。我国第一大岛，属台湾省。面积约3.6万平方千米。。山地纵贯全岛，玉山海拔3952米，是我国东部最高峰。。北部属亚热带，南部属热带。

clips.send: 西沙群岛。位于海南岛东南方。由珊瑚岛礁组成，沙白水清。。永兴岛是南海诸岛中面积最大的岛屿，是海南省三沙市人民政府驻地。

clips.send: 东沙群岛。南海诸岛中位置最北。位于广东东南方的珊瑚岛礁。。南海诸岛包括东沙群岛、西沙群岛、中沙群岛和南沙群岛。

clips.send: 渤海。三面环陆的内海。是我国的内海，三面被辽宁、河北、天津、山东环抱。。海水很浅，平均深度约18米。。面积约7.7万平方千米；冬季北部会结冰。。黄河注入渤海；这里有我国最大的海上油田和长芦盐场。

clips.send: 海南岛。海南省，热带海岛。面积约3.4万平方千米，是我国第二大岛。。终年如夏，有椰林、海滩和橡胶林；三亚在它的南端。。海南省还管辖着南海诸岛。
